checks.finding: requirements.md AC-009 (lines 357-367) states plainly that 'assert_artifacts_schema and assert_terminal (tests/lib/loop-driver.sh, INV-004) are themselves unmodified by this addition' -- i.e. the capability_applicability field addition leaves assert_terminal's body untouched. acceptance-tests.md's TEST-009 row (line 13, the acceptance test for that same AC-009) instead asserts assert_terminal's body has 'one sanctioned change from the pre-T-006 body ... the `_loop_trace_emit done-transition:assert-terminal` call', locked at 'TEST-009.2's re-baselined hash', and frames this as a correction already made in a 'T-005 cycle-2 correction' to a 'prior hash'. Downstream failure: a task author or verifier reading AC-009 alone will conclude assert_terminal must not change at all, while acceptance-tests.md tells them a specific line must already have been inserted via a prior task cycle -- but this package's own Overview and Non-goals state plainly that 'No test code, fixtures, or registry edits are produced by this task' and that tasks.md (where any T-005/T-006 would live) 'follow[s] in a later phase once this package passes spec-review-loop'. There is no tasks.md in this package and acceptance-tests.md's own Test ID column lists only 'TEST-009' (no '.2' variant) for AC-009, so 'TEST-009.2', 'T-005 cycle-2 correction', and 'pre-T-006 body' name objects that do not exist anywhere in this Phase 1 package and cannot be resolved by the artifacts under review. This is a specification-review-scoped defect (a direct inconsistency between requirements.md and acceptance-tests.md, the two primary Phase 1 artifacts this gate reviews) rather than an implementation-review or quality-gate concern, since no code exists yet against which to adjudicate which statement is correct. Severity Critical is the check's mandated severity and is also independently justified: the contradiction leaves AC-009/TEST-009 -- whether assert_terminal's body may or must change -- with two mutually exclusive truth conditions, so this specific requirement cannot be validated as currently written.
